topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out what students should learn about cancer causation.

topics.label: Cancer evolution and the origins of susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations arise and enable cancer evolution within a susceptible cell and a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and evidence for their contribution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the contribution of environmental exposures to cancer risk and how evidence for that contribution should be interpreted.

topics.label: Infectious causes of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive carcinogenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma to develop the interaction between pathogens and tumour development.

topics.label: Environmental carcinogens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental exposures damage DNA, showing how their mutagenic effects depend on chemical activity and metabolism.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish mutational initiation from the conditions that promote tumour outgrowth, grounding that distinction in asbestos exposure and experimental evidence.

topics.label: Biological context and susceptibility to carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the biological context of exposure affects carcinogenic susceptibility and conclude by synthesising the mechanisms already discussed.

topics.label: Tracing carcinogen exposure through mutational signatures
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses how patterns in tumour DNA can provide evidence of prior exposure to particular carcinogens.

topics.label: Methods and limitations of assessing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how carcinogenic potential is investigated and why the available methods cannot fully reproduce or establish human cancer risk.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing draws together the lecture's conclusions about environmental cancer risks and places them within everyday risk–benefit decisions.
